correctness.rationale: Removing the leader gives two Neumann–Dirichlet blocks of lengths j,n−1−j. A cosine eigenvector with components cos((i+1/2)θ), i=0,…,ℓ−1, obeys the reflected left boundary and a zero at i=ℓ exactly for θ=(2r−1)π/(2ℓ+1). This fixes the e^(−tL) normalization. The small-time trace coefficient orders vertices by their original degree; the smallest mode of the longer block, strictly decreasing in that length, orders the eventual fixed-n optimum. For ℓ/√t tending to a positive finite x, 2−2 cos θ≥4θ²/π² gives Gaussian domination, and the scaled eigenvalues give the stated h(x); the same bound sends the block trace to zero when ℓ/√t→0. For ℓ≫√t, midpoint quadrature subtracts ℓc(t) with error O(√t/ℓ)+O(c(t))+O(e^(−3t)): the absolute derivative has one maximum (solve cos θ=2t sin²θ) of order √t, so its total variation is O(√t). The reflected long block obeys this uniformly. Poisson summation gives G(x) and negativity from the alternating series; the correction vanishes at both ends. Independently of the supplied curvature code, each differentiated spectral term contributes 2a x⁻⁶ exp(−a/x²)(2a−3x²)>0 to G″ for 0<x≤1, where a=π²(r+1/2)². For x≥1 the alternate representation of G′ is strictly positive: the first two positive magnitudes have ratio b₂/b₁≤7e⁻³<1, and the rest decrease. A separate exact-rational calculation in evidence/2/root_bracket.py certifies opposite derivative signs at 0.86518 and 0.86519 with absolute omitted-tail bound 144(3/8)^26. The resulting unique negative minimum beats every subsequence escaping to zero or infinity; any remaining subsequential limit of a minimizing distance must equal ξ.
